high.title: Brazil Records US$1.8 Billion Current Account Deficit in April, More Negative Than Market Expected
high.summary: Brazil posted a current account deficit of US$1.765 billion in April, significantly worse than the Reuters consensus expectation of US$200 million deficit. The 12-month accumulated deficit now represents 2.66% of GDP. The primary income account showed a deficit of US$6.801 billion versus US$5.018 billion in April 2025, while the trade balance posted a surplus of US$9.707 billion. The services account deficit widened to US$5.044 billion from US$4.091 billion year-over-year. However, foreign direct investment exceeded expectations, providing some offset. This larger-than-expected current account deficit could pressure the BRL and reinforce concerns about Brazil's external financing needs, particularly important given the elevated global risk environment and potential capital flow volatility.

high.title: Central Bank Sees Increased Global Uncertainty from Middle East Conflict and Higher Risk in Household Credit
high.summary: The Central Bank of Brazil released its Financial Stability Report highlighting increased external uncertainty in H2 2025 driven by the US-Israel-Iran conflict. Geopolitical tensions have significantly elevated global risks, particularly impacting the Middle East region and supply chains, including commodity flows through the Strait of Hormuz. Despite this, the BCB notes that global growth in 2025 surprised positively even amid policy uncertainties and rising US tariffs. The report emphasizes that external funding supply to Brazil's financial system remains robust and above demand, with no relevant short-term cost pressures. Domestically, the National Financial System's profitability remained stable in H2. This assessment suggests the BCB is closely monitoring external risks that could impact monetary policy decisions and BRL stability, while domestic financial conditions remain supportive.

medium.title: Ibovespa Falls with Risk Aversion Focused on Middle East; 5 Things to Know Before Investing Today (26)
medium.summary: The Ibovespa opened Tuesday down 0.93% to 176,154 points due to renewed risk aversion following US attacks on Iran. USD/BRL traded down 0.12% to R$5.0131 while the DXY fell 0.11%. The market is also monitoring progress on the proposal to end the 6x1 work schedule in Congress, with the Chamber of Deputies postponing the vote after a collective review request.

medium.title: Ibovespa Rises with Optimism Over US-Iran Agreement; 5 Things to Know Before Investing Today (25)
medium.summary: The Ibovespa opened Monday up 0.32% to 176,770 points, following external optimism over evolving negotiations for a peace agreement between the US and Iran. USD/BRL fell 0.47% to R$5.0048 while the DXY declined 0.30%. A new BTG Pactual/Nexus poll shows President Lula leading Senator Flávio Bolsonaro 47% to 43% in a hypothetical second round, within the margin of error.

medium.title: Empiricus Issues 'Alert' on Its Recommended Stocks to Seek Extra Income: Petrobras (PETR4) and Vale (VALE3) Are Highlighted
medium.summary: After weeks of optimism, Brazil's domestic market entered a more delicate phase in May, with the Ibovespa falling from near 200,000 points in April to around 177,000 currently. Selic rate expectations also deteriorated, with the market expecting rates to end 2026 at 13.25% annually according to the latest Focus report. Empiricus analysts note that corrections after significant rallies are normal, but additional challenging elements are making the scenario more difficult.

medium.title: CADE Superintendence Recommends Rejection of B3's 60% CRDC Acquisition (B3SA3)
medium.summary: CADE's General Superintendence recommended rejection of B3's R$15 million acquisition of 60% of CRDC (Central de Registro de Direitos Creditórios). The case was classified as "complex" in March, requiring deeper analysis of conglomerate effects and rivalry impacts. The recommendation now goes to CADE's tribunal for final decision.
